== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L109-L175
   109  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
   110                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
   111                 [--dump-decls OUT]
   112                 FILE.ndjson
   113         con-ron --help
   114  
   115    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: if
   116                      the declaration fold accepts a stream in this mode, the
   117                      environment holds no constant whose type is False
   118                      (ConLeche.no_proof_of_False, and DESIGN.md §1's
   119                      conron.no_proof_of_False for the port).
   120    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   121                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   122                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   123    --jobs=<n>        the check phase's worker count: <n> workers claim records
   124                      one at a time off a shared counter, and --jobs=1 runs the
   125                      plain loop with no counter and no result table.  The
   126                      verdict, and the declaration a rejection names, are the
   127                      same at every <n>: the results are walked in RECORD order,
   128                      so the first failing record in fold order is the one
   129                      reported.  Each worker reserves 1 GiB of address space for
   130                      its stack, so a run under `ulimit -v` needs 3x the
   131                      checker's resident set plus a gigabyte per worker; the
   132                      DEFAULT is one worker per hardware thread capped at 16 for
   133                      that reason (con-leche's uncapped default aborts on a
   134                      96-thread machine).  0 or a non-numeral is a usage error,
   135                      as in con-leche.
   136    --no-mark-persistent
   137                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP: the mark it turns off is a
   138                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   139                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this program's counts are
   140                      std::sync::Arc counts -- atomic by type, in every lane,
   141                      with no runtime mark to clear.  A run that passes it says
   142                      so on stderr.
   143    --progress[=<stride>]
   144                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   145                      phase:
   146                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   147                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   148                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> checks pending t=<s>s
   149                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   150                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   151                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s, <n> workers
   152                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   153                      declaration is installed (<i> is its FOLD position, which
   154                      the stream's record index sits near but not at a fixed
   155                      offset above), so a run that dies in the install phase
   156                      names the declaration it died in on its last line.  A
   157                      check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th COMPLETED
   158                      check.  On a failure the phase's closing line says so
   159                      ('install failed at', 'check failed at') and the summary
   160                      still prints.  Bare --progress is stride 1; a stride that
   161                      is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is a usage error.
   162    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   163                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   164                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.
   165    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   166                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   167                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   168                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   169                      verified core and decoded by it.
   170    --dump-decls OUT  con-ron's own: write the parsed declaration list in the
   171                      `con-ron-decls/1` format and exit, without folding.
   172    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   173                      position; no input is read.
   174  
   175  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L40-L45
    40  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    41  //! |---|---|---|
    42  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the stream's declaration records |
    43  //! | 1 | `rejected` | a declaration is invalid |
    44  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |
    45  //! | 3 | error | bad usage, malformed input, or an internal failure of unclear cause |

     2  //! dump instead of a raw stream.

    14  //!               FILE.decls

== scripts/setup-aeneas-lean.sh#L1-L14
     1  #!/usr/bin/env bash
     2  # Produce `_tmp/aeneas-lean/`: a copy of `vendor/aeneas/backends/lean` with
     3  # `patches/aeneas-433.patch` applied, so that the Aeneas Lean library
     4  # builds on con-leche's toolchain (leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0 + Mathlib v4.33.0).
     5  # See DESIGN.md, task #2.
     6  #
     7  # Idempotent: a stamp records the patch's and the source tree's hashes; a
     8  # second run with nothing changed is a no-op and, crucially, keeps the
     9  # existing `.lake/` (rebuilding Mathlib's dependents costs minutes).
    10  #
    11  # Exits non-zero if the patch does not apply cleanly to the pinned Aeneas
    12  # submodule -- that is the signal that the submodule moved and the patch needs
    13  # rebasing.
    14  #

   430      let df: u64 = data(&f);
   431      let da: u64 = data(&a);

   438          max_u64(bvar_of_data(df), bvar_of_data(da)),

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/core_c.rs#L5089-L5120
  5089  pub fn whnf_core(
  5090      mode: &CheckMode,
  5091      fuel: u64,
  5092      st: &mut CState,
  5093      fe: &FEnv,
  5094      d: u64,
  5095      e: &Expr,
  5096  ) -> CheckM<Expr> {
  5097      const M: [u32; 24] = [
  5098          102, 117, 101, 108, 32, 101, 120, 104, 97, 117, 115, 116, 101, 100, 58, 32, 119, 104,
  5099          110, 102, 67, 111, 114, 101,
  5100      ];
  5101      if fuel == 0 {
  5102          Err(core_types::internal(core_types::code_points(&M)))
  5103      } else {
  5104          match whnf_core_probe(st, e) {
  5105              Some(r) => Ok(r),
  5106              None => match whnf_core_body_i(mode, fuel - 1, st, fe, d, e) {
  5107                  Err(err) => Err(err),
  5108                  Ok(r) => {
  5109                      st.whnf_core_c.insert(expr::dup(e), expr::dup(&r));
  5110                      Ok(r)
  5111                  }
  5112              },
  5113          }
  5114      }
  5115  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/checker_c.rs#L123-L132
   123  pub fn or_else_step(attempt: CheckM<bool>) -> OrElseStep {
   124      match attempt {
   125          Ok(true) => OrElseStep::Matched,
   126          Ok(false) => OrElseStep::Continue,
   127          Err(e) => match e {
   128              CheckError::Native(m) => OrElseStep::Failed(CheckError::Native(m)),
   129              _ => OrElseStep::Recovered(e),
   130          },
   131      }
   132  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/installed.rs#L728-L760
   728  pub fn check_decls(
   729      mode: &CheckMode,
   730      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,
   731      ds: &Vec<DeclC>,
   732  ) -> Result<Env, (CheckError, u64)> {
   733      // `.0` on the spot, so the visited set is dropped **here** rather than at
   734      // the end of the function: a binding that held the whole tuple would keep
   735      // one table entry per distinct node alive for the length of the fold, and
   736      // that is 0.5 GB of peak RSS at `Init` scale for nothing (task #73).
   737      let ok: bool = validate::validate_decls(validate::seen_new(), ds).0;
   738      if ok {
   739          check_decls_go(mode, pins, ds)
   740      } else {
   741          Err((core_types::native(validate_reject_message()), 0))
   742      }
   743  }
   744  
   745  /// con-leche: none — task #73, the port's own input check (con-leche's computed fields are correct by construction)
   746  /// The decline the validation pass produces.  Its own function so that
   747  /// `check_decls`' two branches are each one call, which is what lets
   748  /// `Refine/Validate.lean` state the gate (`check_decls_gate`) without naming
   749  /// the fold's body.
   750  pub fn validate_reject_message() -> Vec<u32> {
   751      const M: [u32; 49] = [
   752          100, 101, 99, 108, 97, 114, 97, 116, 105, 111, 110, 32, 114, 101, 106, 101, 99,
   753          116, 101, 100, 32, 98, 121, 32, 116, 104, 101, 32, 105, 110, 112, 117, 116, 32,
   754          118, 97, 108, 105, 100, 97, 116, 105, 111, 110, 32, 112, 97, 115, 115,
   755      ];
   756      core_types::code_points(&M)
   757  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/kernel/validate.rs#L427-L440
   427  pub fn validate_expr(m: Seen, e: &Expr) -> (bool, Seen) {
   428      let key: u64 = expr::hash(e);
   429      if seen_hit(&m, key, e) {
   430          (true, m)
   431      } else {
   432          let r: (bool, Seen) = validate_expr_arm(m, e);
   433          if r.0 {
   434              (true, seen_record(r.1, key, e))
   435          } else {
   436              (false, r.1)
   437          }
   438      }
   439  }
   440  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/kernel/validate.rs#L812-L830
   812  pub fn validate_decls(m: Seen, ds: &Vec<DeclC>) -> (bool, Seen) {
   813      validate_decls_from(m, ds, 0)
   814  }
   815  
   816  /// con-leche: none — task #73, the port's own input check (con-leche's computed fields are correct by construction)
   817  /// The index recursion behind `validate_decls`.  The visited set is threaded
   818  /// across declarations, which is what makes the pass linear in the *stream's*
   819  /// distinct nodes rather than in each declaration's.
   820  pub fn validate_decls_from(m: Seen, ds: &Vec<DeclC>, i: usize) -> (bool, Seen) {
   821      if i >= ds.len() {
   822          (true, m)
   823      } else {
   824          let r: (bool, Seen) = validate_decl(m, &ds[i]);
   825          if r.0 {
   826              validate_decls_from(r.1, ds, i + 1)
   827          } else {
   828              (false, r.1)
   829          }
   830      }

   643    constTyAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_ty_at lst.constTyAt
   644      absNameLevels absExpr
   645    constValAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_val_at lst.constValAt
   646      absNameLevels absExpr

   648      absNameNameLevels absExpr
   649    whnfCoreC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_core_c lst.whnfCoreC absExpr absExpr
   650    whnfC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_c lst.whnfC absExpr absExpr
   651    inferC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_c lst.inferC absExpr absExpr
   652    inferIOC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_io_c lst.inferIOC absExpr absExpr
   653    defeqC : HashMap.RelOn ExprPairWF st.defeq_c lst.defeqC absExprPair id
   654    annotC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.annot_c lst.annotC absExpr absExpr
   655    lsimpC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lsimp_c lst.lsimpC absLevel absLevel
   656    lnzC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lnz_c lst.lnzC absLevel id
   657    eqvC : HashMap.RelOn LevelPairWF st.eqv_c lst.eqvC absLevelPair id
   658    instC : HashMap.RelOn InstKeyWF st.inst_c lst.instC absInstKey absExpr
   659    /-- The `instC` table's **entry count**, which the other thirteen clauses do
   660    not need: `StateRel` is a lookup agreement and a lookup agreement does not
   661    bound the Lean map's size.  `cached::state_c::inst_list_m` is the one
   662    operation that reads a count — the `instC` entry cap, `inst_c.len() <
   663    inst_c_cap_c` against `mp.size < instCCapC` (`StateC.lean:186-199`) — so
   664    without this clause the two sides can disagree about whether the table is
   665    full.  Task #61 folded it in (`Refine/StateC.lean` had it as a free-standing
   666    `InstCSize` hypothesis that nothing could discharge). -/
   667    instCSize : (HashMap.al_v st.inst_c).length = lst.instC.size
   668  
   669  /-- The port-side invariant of the fourteen tables: each is a well-formed
   670  `ron::HashMap` (task #16's `Inv`) holding only well-formed keys and — where the

== proof/ConRon/Refine/Abs.lean#L511-L525
   511  inductive ExprWF : expr.Expr → Prop where
   512    | bvar {i e} : expr.bvar i = ok e → ExprWF e
   513    | fvar {idx ty e} : ExprWF ty → expr.fvar idx ty = ok e → ExprWF e
   514    | sort {u e} : LevelWF u → expr.sort u = ok e → ExprWF e
   515    | mk_const {n us e} : NameWF n → LevelsWF us → expr.mk_const n us = ok e → ExprWF e
   516    | app {f a e} : ExprWF f → ExprWF a → expr.app f a = ok e → ExprWF e
   517    | lam {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   518        expr.lam ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   519    | forall_e {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   520        expr.forall_e ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   521    | let_e {ty v b e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF v → ExprWF b →
   522        expr.let_e ty v b = ok e → ExprWF e
   523    | lit {l e} : LiteralWF l → expr.lit l = ok e → ExprWF e
   524    | proj {s i x e} : NameWF s → ExprWF x → expr.proj s i x = ok e → ExprWF e
   525

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv
   903        have h0 : f = 0#u64 := u64_val_inj (by rw [hfv]; rfl)
   904        subst h0; exact wrappers_zero mode
   905      | succ n ih =>
   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
